title: Condensed exceptional inverse image of a reconstructed finite-level system
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. On a scheme $T$ equal to $X$ or $Y$, write $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}=\varprojlim_n (\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$, and let $\mathcal I_T$ be the completed integral constructible category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$. Its rationalization has morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Let $J_T:\mathcal I_T[1/\ell]\simeq\mathcal C^c_E(T)$ be the scalar-extension realization of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Let $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ and $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous maps on the profinite set $S$ with values in one finite intermediate field of $\Omega/E$, as in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category, prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Define the functor
$$U_T:\mathcal I_T\longrightarrow\mathcal C^c_\Omega(T),\qquad U_T(L)=\Omega_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}J_T(L[1/\ell]).$$

For $L\in\mathcal I_Y$ put $L_n=L\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,Y}}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_Y$. Let $Rf_n^!$ denote the constructible exceptional inverse image obtained from the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint by site comparison, as explicitly constructed for arbitrary $k$ in [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons]. Suppose supplied a strict semilinear derived tower $M_\bullet\in D(\mathscr S_X)$, where $\mathscr S_X$ is the abelian coefficient-system category of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and use its underlying completed-coefficient tower in taking $R\varprojlim$. It has specified level identifications $\phi_n:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$, normalization isomorphisms $M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1,X}}A_{n,X}\simeq M_n$, transitions induced by these isomorphisms and the quotient maps, and the quotient cocycle, where $A_{n,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$. Require that the $\phi_n$ intertwine these transitions with the exceptional-image quotient transitions. In addition require either (a) the $\phi_n$ are the evaluations of a specified identification of normalized derived systems with the exceptional section $G(\mathcal R_YL)$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates, lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], or (b) there is one integer $r$ such that every $M_n$ has cohomology only in degree $r$. In case (b) no enhanced identification or section counit is additional input: the comparison is defined by the functorial good-truncation identification of each system with its degree-$r$ cohomology diagram, and the strict isomorphism of cohomology diagrams induced by the $\phi_n$. In either case the section counit is the geometric section counit transported through that identification. Suppose each cohomology sheaf of each level is constructible in the intrinsic finite-stratification sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and the levels have a common finite cohomological interval independent of $n$. Assume $M=R\varprojlim M_\bullet$ lies in $\mathcal I_X$, with its canonical reductions identified with $M_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then there is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{f,L,M_\bullet}:U_X(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,\Omega}^{\,R}(U_YL).$$
Here $Rf_{!,\Omega}$ is the bounded constructible condensed-module compact-support functor, defined using extension by zero and proper direct image in the chosen Nagata compactification [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], and $Rf_{!,\Omega}^{\,R}$ is its chosen right adjoint on $\mathcal C^c_\Omega$, namely the functor $Rf^!$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek] for the condensed ring $\underline\Omega$, that is $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleUpperShriek}(\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell),\ell,f)$ at master commit 7347520d9b0d17cc31d0fc34ea20f1381a83fe13. More explicitly, fix the chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ and a right adjoint of its bounded constructible proper direct image $Rg_{*,\Omega}$, as required by the master declaration's left-adjoint instance. Then this right adjoint is $(Rg_{*,\Omega})^R$ followed by $j^*$, with the adjunction obtained by composing $j_!\dashv j^*$ and the chosen $Rg_{*,\Omega}\dashv(Rg_{*,\Omega})^R$. This assertion concerns this constructible right adjoint and asserts no unbounded ambient pro-etale adjoint. The isomorphism is the adjunction comparison: its counit is induced by the finite-level exceptional counits under completed reconstruction, localization and extension to $\Omega$. It is compatible with a refinement of the compactification and with morphisms of the supplied coherent systems. Here such a morphism consists of a map of integral inputs and an actual derived-system map commuting with the identifications with the geometric exceptional sections. In case (b), for two data sets concentrated in the same degree r, commutation of the level-identification squares suffices for this system compatibility, because maps between degree-r cohomology diagrams are determined componentwise. In addition $U_T$ sends the integral coefficient object to the condensed tensor unit and commutes with shifts.

source.place: Agent-formulated comparison obligation for the exact master functors: boundedConstructibleUpperShriekOfCompactification (lines 100–118), boundedConstructibleUpperShriek and its adjunction (lines 128–146), commit 7347520d9b0d17cc31d0fc34ea20f1381a83fe13. Full verbatim source and its imported coefficient definitions are supplied in report.md. Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.14–15 motivates the realization but does not state or prove this condensed-adjoint comparison.

proof.text: Work first over a finite coefficient field $E$, initially $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$. The schemes are qcqs, locally noetherian and finite-dimensional by the three geometric tools cited. A finite affine subcover of a noetherian affine cover makes them noetherian; $\ell$ is invertible since $\operatorname{char}k\ne\ell$. For any $K\in\mathcal I_T(R)$, its stratified-perfect description gives local bounded finite-projective $R$-complexes $P$. Each stratum is quasi-compact; the definition of pro-etale covering selects finitely many affine pieces from its trivializing cover. Take the extreme support degrees of these finitely many $P$, over the finitely many strata, to obtain $[a,b]$. Every reduction is locally represented by $P\otimes_R R/t^n$, a complex of direct summands of finite free coefficient sheaves, hence flat, supported in $[a,b]$. The bounded-above-flat theorem makes it K-flat, so derived change of rings and tensor are computed on this model. For the zero object or empty scheme choose $a=b=0$. For any degree-zero finite-coefficient module sheaf $V$, tensor-pullback identifies the restricted $K_n\otimes^L V$ with this bounded flat model tensored with the restricted $V$. Covering-family detection gives vanishing outside $[a,b]$ on each stratum. Write each stratum as a difference of two closed subsets and successively split along those finitely many closed subsets and their open complements. Every final piece lies in a stratum; the open-closed short exact sequence detects zero sheaves across each split. Reversing the splits proves the same vanishing on $T$. Thus all reductions of $K$ have finite Tor amplitude, uniformly in $n$. Apply this to $L$, the assumed $M$, and every integral test object. Their compatible etale-origin witnesses are part of membership in $\mathcal I_T(R)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11: stratified locally perfect description; elementary finite-cover and open-closed assembly of the Tor interval, using the cited K-flat and locality tools.

proof.text: For A_n=R/t^n, take the enhanced finite categories C_n=D^b_ctf(X,A_n), D_n=D^b_ctf(Y,A_n). The finite geometric comparison lemma gives F_n=Rf_!,n, its right adjoint G_n=Rf_n^!, the coherent equivalences q for reduction, and invertible mates b defined by the counit formula in that lemma. The semilinear section theorem supplies simultaneous enhanced models for open extension, proper pushforward and q. The cartesian-section adjoint-mate theorem therefore applies: F and G act on normalized sections, the exceptional section is G(R_Y L), and H_Y(F R_X K,R_Y L) is isomorphic to H_X(R_X K,G R_Y L) as a derived inverse system of mapping complexes, with the specified counit and all composition coherences. Write N_bullet=G(R_Y L) in D(S_X), with its actual geometric section counit. The next step constructs the required identification with M_bullet under either alternative in the statement.

source.place: sk-prop-sp-integral-adjunction/first paragraph: adjunction on normalized towers

proof.text: Write $N_\bullet=G(\mathcal R_YL)$. In case (a), take the supplied identification $\theta:M_\bullet\simeq N_\bullet$. In case (b), evaluation is exact in $\mathscr S_X$, so both systems have cohomology only in degree $r$. For a representative $C$ of either system, the functorial good truncations give quasi-isomorphisms $C\leftarrow\tau_{\le r}C\to H^r(C)[-r]$. The second arrow is the quotient $\ker d^r\to\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$ in degree $r$ and zero in lower degrees. The cohomology concentration theorem identifies their images in the derived category. The commuting transition squares for $\phi_n$ give an isomorphism $H^r(M_\bullet)\simeq H^r(N_\bullet)$ of actual semilinear sheaf systems. Conjugating its shifted single-complex map by these zigzags gives $\theta$. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero single functor, followed by shift, implies that its evaluation is exactly $\phi_n$: both maps induce $H^r(\phi_n)$. The same full faithfulness proves naturality for maps of two data sets in the same degree $r$. For case (a) morphisms, naturality is the required square with the supplied identifications. Transport the geometric section counit through $\theta$; this constructs the coherent counit without lifting arbitrary levelwise derived maps.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations: functorial good truncations; single-degree comparison in the abelian system category

proof.text:
Let K be any object of I_X(R), and let P_R be the compact-support reconstruction functor. Its comparison alpha identifies R_Y(P_R K) with F R_X K as normalized derived systems. Write L_T for the total-limit functor of the system evaluation calculus. That calculus, the preceding mapping-system adjunction and alpha give the natural chain
RHom_X(K,M) = RHom_X(K,L_X M_bullet) ≃ Rlim H_X(R_X K,M_bullet) ≃ Rlim H_Y(F R_X K,R_Y L) ≃ RHom_Y(P_R K,L_Y R_Y L) ≃ RHom_Y(P_R K,L).
The last arrow uses the actual derived-completeness isomorphism L→L_Y R_Y L in the definition of I_Y. These are isomorphisms of derived mapping complexes; take H^0 only after forming the displayed chain. This gives R-linear, natural inverse bijections Hom_X(K,M)≃Hom_Y(P_R K,L). The projection identities for gamma and the section adjunction show that the image of id_M is a morphism P_R M→L whose coherent reductions, conjugated by alpha and the supplied reduction identification, are exactly epsilon_n:F_n M_n→L_n. This is a statement about the specified derived-system map; equality is not deduced from equality of evaluations of arbitrary morphisms.

source.place: sk-prop-sp-integral-adjunction/displayed chain of Hom bijections and final counit paragraph

proof.text:
Tensor the R-linear inverse Hom bijections of Step 4 with E. The raw rationalized categories have precisely these tensor Hom groups, and exact linear functors and their transformations extend to them by h/t^r↦F(h)/t^r. Thus the same bijection holds on rationalized integral categories, with its same counit. Apply the E-linear equivalences J_X,J_Y and the compact-support comparison a. Every C in C_E^c(X) has a lattice by the realization theorem, so this yields, naturally in all C,
Hom_E(C,J_X(M[1/t])) ≃ Hom_E(P_E^c C,J_Y(L[1/t])).
This is the assertion that J_X M represents this Hom functor at the supplied L. No global integral right-adjoint preservation theorem over an algebraically closed finite field is being applied to k.

source.place: sk-prop-sp-rational/localized Hom formula and scalar extension of the integral adjunction

proof.text: For a finite extension $E\subset F$, put $S=\mathcal O_F$, with uniformizer $v$ and ramification index $e$. Form $L_S=L\otimes^L_{\widehat R}\widehat S$ and $M_S=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R}\widehat S$. The finite-free completed-scalar theorem identifies these with the completed integral scalar extensions, including their canonical quotient maps and total limits. The integral scalar-extension theorem, together with the stratified-perfect characterization identifying its integral category with $\mathcal I(S)$, puts them in $\mathcal I_Y(S)$ and $\mathcal I_X(S)$. Tensor associativity identifies their $S/v^m$ reductions with $L\otimes^L_{\widehat R}S/v^m$ and $M\otimes^L_{\widehat R}S/v^m$. Apply enhanced coefficient extension to the actual $\theta$ of Step 3 on $S/t^nS=S/v^{en}$ and then the finite-free exceptional mate. This is an equivalence of enhanced systems with the exceptional system of $L_S$ on these cofinal levels. Its counit is the extended section counit, by the equation defining the mate $b$. This supplies coherent data, even when the single-degree alternative no longer holds after a nonflat quotient.

source.place: sk-thm-sp-qbar/finite-field coefficient compatibility before taking Hom colimits

proof.text:
For every $m$ choose $n$ with $en\ge m$. Reduce the preceding equivalence at $S/v^{en}$ to $S/v^m$, then compose with the exceptional quotient mate. The quotient cocycle and mixed coefficient diagrams of the finite comparison theorem identify the results for two choices of $n$ by first passing to a common larger $n$; the same equations give the transition square for two $m$ and preserve the counits. Thus this is an enhanced identification of the full $v$-adic exceptional system, providing alternative (a) over $F$. Steps 1–5, applied over $F$, now give natural inverse bijections for every $C_F\in\mathcal C_F^c(X)$:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_F(C_F,T_{E,F}J_XM)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_F(P_F^cC_F,T_{E,F}J_YL).$$
Here $J_F(M_S[1/v])\simeq T_{E,F}J_E(M[1/t])$ is tensor associativity for the scalar-extension definition of $J$, and likewise for $L$. The compact-support scalar comparisons identify the left functors. The mate counit equation, tensor associativity and the compact-support coefficient coherences identify these bijections under a further extension $F\subset H$; both transposes are the extension of the same counit. This covers every finite-stage test object, not only extensions of $E$-objects.

source.place: sk-thm-sp-qbar/compatibility with finite extension before the displayed colimit adjunction

proof.text:
Return to E=Q_ell. An arbitrary C in C_Omega^c(X) descends to some C_F at a finite F/E by the filtered two-colimit theorem. Each Hom from C to U_X M is the filtered colimit, over finite H containing F, of Hom_H(T_FH C_F,T_EH J_E M); this is precisely the morphism description in that theorem. Apply the compatible bijections of Step 7 at H. The compact-support scalar comparison identifies P_H T_FH C_F with T_FH P_F C_F, and identifies P_Omega C with T_FOmega P_F C_F. The resulting colimit on the other side is Hom_Omega(P_Omega C,U_Y L), by the same two-colimit theorem. The inverse maps commute with the transition maps as well, so their filtered colimits are inverse. Descent of morphisms and eventual equality give naturality independently of the chosen finite field and descended object. We have therefore constructed
Hom_Omega(C,U_X M) ≃ Hom_Omega(P_Omega C,U_Y L)
for every C, with counit t:P_Omega U_X M→U_Y L obtained from the finite-stage counits. This argument uses the finite-extension-valued Omega coefficient ring, not the full ring of all continuous Omega-valued functions.

source.place: sk-thm-sp-qbar/displayed filtered Hom colimits and descent of naturality

proof.text: Let R be the exact chosen bounded-constructible right adjoint of P_Omega specified in the statement and the archived master, and let epsilon^R be its counit. Define c:U_X M→R(U_Y L) to be the adjoint transpose of t. For every C, postcomposition by c is the Step 8 representation followed by the chosen adjunction bijection, hence is bijective. In particular choose r:R(U_Y L)→U_X M mapping to id_R; then c r=id_R. Injectivity with C=U_X M implies r c=id, so c is an isomorphism and epsilon^R∘P_Omega(c)=t. For a map of supplied coherent systems, naturality of the representation implies the corresponding square for c, since both composites have the same adjoint transpose. For a compactification refinement write q:P^1→P^2 for its compact-support comparison and R^1,R^2 for the chosen right adjoints. Define rho:R^2→R^1 by transposing epsilon^2 composed with q_(R^2); transposing q inverse gives its inverse, by the two adjunction triangle identities. The finite geometric counit and compact-support refinement coherences in Steps 2–8 give t^1=t^2 composed with q_(U_X M). The two maps c^1 and rho composed with c^2 therefore have this same transpose, and are equal. This is the required refinement square. This proves compatibility of the specified comparison, rather than merely abstract isomorphism of the two objects.

source.place: sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint/counit transposes and the two inverse identities

proof.text: Finally J_T is derived extension from the completed integral ring, so it takes that ring to E_T^c: multiplication gives B tensor_A A≃B with inverse b↦b tensor 1. Extending once more to Omega gives U_T(Rhat_T)≃Omega_T^c, the condensed tensor unit. J_T and derived coefficient extension commute with shifts; the latter is explicitly computed by exact termwise tensor. Their composite U_T therefore commutes with shifts, with the usual coherent shift identifications.
